blocks.title: Mechanics
blocks.subtitle: How the peril works, how the score works — briefly, before the full case.

blocks.text: The frame
Exposure against Preparedness

Every entity is placed on two scored axes. Exposure measures the size of the bet: how much non-firm, curtailable load sits in the book or the asset, how concentrated it is on the same grid geography, and how badly today's wordings miss the peril. Preparedness measures the ability to carry it: whether the underwriter has the data, the products, the modelling, the expertise and the capital to actually hold the risk it has written.

blocks.caption: The two axes cut the field into four quadrants. The warning light is a large negative margin.

cells.label: Whitespace
cells.note: Capable, under-deployed. Capacity is available here but not yet earning — the opportunity.

cells.label: Earning it
cells.note: Exposed and prepared. Carrying real non-firm risk with the data, products and capital to match.

cells.label: Sidelined
cells.note: Neither exposed nor ready. Watching from the bench while the market forms.

cells.label: Exposed
cells.note: Exposure accumulating faster than the data, products and capital to support it. The danger zone.

blocks.text: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure. Not who is exposed? — who is exposed beyond their ability to carry it?
How interruption works
Why interruption is not damage

A non-firm connection fails in a way the market's instruments do not register. There is no broken asset, no proximate physical cause, no repair. The grid operator, acting entirely within its rights, instructs a curtailment; the facility loses availability; the penalty or the lost revenue lands. A business-interruption policy that triggers on physical damage to insured property{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI}} never sees it.

Curtailment is a compound loss{{cite:ACT-COMP-LOSS}} — frequency times severity — and both terms move with grid constraints and queue position, not with the asset's physical condition. Covering it means a trigger that pays on an index of interruption rather than a loss adjuster's finding of damage, with the basis risk{{cite:ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES,ACAD-TEH-WOOLNOUGH-TRIGGER}} that any parametric line inherits.
Why cat and cyber miss it
A catastrophe model needs a physical hazard footprint; curtailment has none — the hazard is in the connection agreement and the constraint map.{{cite:LLOYDS-RDS}}
Cyber underwriters learned to price a non-physical peril, but aggregation runs through shared software and service providers — not shared grid geography.{{cite:ACAD-AI-ENERGY-DCC}}

Non-firm power risk correlates through the network: two data centres behind the same constraint boundary move together whether or not they share code.{{cite:ACAD-CCM-NF-LOAD}} Any serious attempt to price it starts with registers that describe the grid, not an imported event set.
How we score

Every rating names its source class — register, filing, derived field, or sourced research — and links to the primary. Outside-in judgements fuse with register readings by published credibility rules;{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}} where registers are still landing, magnitudes stay directional until measured share clears the L5 threshold. Full scoring pipeline: methodology.
With the map and the mechanics set: three claims, one instrument.

blocks.title: Argument & proposal
blocks.subtitle: Substantiate the case, name the instrument, close on who can carry what the market has not yet priced.

blocks.text: The case
A peril the market was not built to see

For a century the large industrial insurance contract has answered a single question: what happens if the thing breaks? That question built the property and business-interruption market. It is also, increasingly, the wrong one for the fastest-growing concentration of insured value in Britain. The dominant risk to a data centre or a grid-scale energy asset is no longer that it breaks. It is that it is lawfully, contractually, and repeatedly switched off.{{cite:ACAD-DC-OUTAGE}}

This essay makes three claims and proposes one instrument. First, that non-firm power risk is large, growing, and structurally mispriced. Second, that the models the market reaches for cannot see it, for reasons that are architectural rather than incidental. Third, that pricing it correctly requires the two-axis construct above — exposure against preparedness — not a single hazard score. The instrument is an outside-in map of exactly that, reconciled from the registers and filings the placement chain already walks past.
The economics
Why the number is large

The data-centre build-out has put a demand queue measured in the tens of gigawatts in front of the system operator,{{cite:ACAD-DESANTI-FCA-QUEUE}} and the connections clearing it are disproportionately the flexible, curtailable kind. A hyperscale facility contracts for tens to hundreds of megawatts and sells its tenants a four-nines availability SLA — roughly 52 minutes of permitted downtime a year. A sustained curtailment is a direct breach, and power is already the single largest cause of significant data-centre outages.{{cite:ACAD-DC-OUTAGE,INDUSTRY-DC-COMPUTE-DEMAND}}

The financial value at risk is contracted load times hours off times the penalty rate per hour. None of those terms appears in a physical-damage policy. The market is therefore carrying an exposure whose severity it does not compute and whose frequency it does not track. The premium that should attach to availability cover is a function the existing book never evaluates; the premium that does attach is zero, because the cover does not exist.
The market is not underpricing this peril. It is not pricing it at all.
The proposal
A wedge, not a data vendor

The cat-model instinct is to reduce a risk to a single number and rank the market by it. For this peril that instinct misranks the field. The same non-firm exposure is well-carried by an underwriter with the data, products, modelling and capital to hold it, and dangerous in the hands of one without. A one-axis score cannot express that, because it collapses the two things whose difference is the entire signal.

The index is a wedge: the proprietary, primary-source understanding of a peril the rest of the market underwrites blind. The measured features — connection-gate status, flexible-connection share, aggregation over shared grid geography, trigger gap against parametric availability — are built to be exactly the edge that lets you price the gap and carry it. Whoever holds that picture first is positioned not to sell a score, but to write the cover that does not yet exist.
The re-pricing
Rules that turn firmness into a fact

Connections reform is converting firmness into a dated, registered fact. As the queue moves to a gated model, an asset's firmness becomes an objective register entry: which gate it sits behind, on what terms, with what curtailment rights attached.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,ACAD-DESANTI-FCA-QUEUE}} Live rules such as CMP434/448 and GC0166 start re-pricing the same sub-factors on every renewal.
The opportunity
Whoever can measure it can carry it

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

The market deploys capacity onto whoever looks exposed on a damage view, while genuine non-firm losses concentrate where exposure has outrun preparedness — and the genuinely capable sit in under-priced whitespace. The rankings and profiles below test whether that divergence shows up in the live data.
